title: [YouPass Collect] - Satisfaction Levels of Full-Time and Part-Time Students About University Library Services
prompt: The charts below show the results of a survey conducted by a university library to find out the opinions of full-time and part-time students about its services. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The four pie charts illustrate the levels of satisfaction among full-time and part-time university students regarding two library services, namely IT support and opening hours.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, while both student groups expressed high levels of contentment with the library's opening hours, opinions on IT support were far more divided, with part-time students being notably less satisfied. In addition, full-time students were generally happier with the services provided than their part-time counterparts.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding IT support, a clear majority of full-time students were very happy with this service, at 55%, compared to only a fifth of part-time students. Conversely, nearly half of part-time attendees reported being not at all satisfied, which was over three times higher than the figure for full-time students, at just 13%. Meanwhile, the proportion of students who were quite happy was relatively similar between the two groups, at 32% and 35% for full-time and part-time students, respectively.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for the library's opening hours, satisfaction levels were considerably higher for both groups. Approximately two-thirds and nearly three-quarters of full-time and part-time students, respectively, were very pleased with the current schedule. A further 32% of full-time students expressed moderate satisfaction, which was 9 percentage points higher than the corresponding figure for part-time attendees. Notably, dissatisfaction was minimal in both cases, with only 1% of full-time and 5% of part-time students reporting that they were not at all happy with this service.
